what: a bounded numerical reproduction of the quadratic rough Heston model as OptionStratLib 0.24 implements it, against values the papers state; fixed before anything runs

papers.market_making: Rosenbaum and Zhang, Multi-asset market making under the quadratic rough Heston, arXiv:2212.10164v1
papers.calibration: Rosenbaum and Zhang, Deep calibration of the quadratic rough Heston model, arXiv:2107.01611 (reference [28] of the first, the source of its kernel)

declared: the parameters are the papers' SPX values, used as such; they are calibrated to nothing here and never stand for BTC or any other market

only the SPX part is reproduced: VIX futures and options under the model, the joint SPX/VIX calibration and the neural pricing of the papers are out of scope (OptionStratLib has no VIX pricing or calibration under the model; issues are opened there)
the market making results of 2212.10164 are figures of value functions and controls, not numbers; they are not reproduced in step 1

model.source: 2107.01611 Appendix A: geometric partition with x*_10 = 3.92 at alpha = 0.51 (Figure A.1), n = 10 (Section 2.2)

kernel_weights.what: OptionStratLib's (c_i, gamma_i) for alpha 0.51, n 10, x_n 3.92 against the closed form of 2107.01611 Appendix A, computed independently here
kernel_weights.pass: every c_i and gamma_i equal to the closed form within a relative 1e-10

optimal_ratio.what: argmin over x_n > 1 of the L2(0, 0.1) distance between K^n and the fractional kernel, for n = 10
optimal_ratio.pass: within 0.02 of each printed value (they are printed to two decimals)

initial_variance.what: V0 = a (Z0 - b)^2 + c with Z0 = sum c_i z0_i
initial_variance.pass: equal to 0.18 when rounded to two decimals

monte_carlo.what: OptionStratLib's Monte Carlo vanilla prices at the 2212.10164 parameters, spot 3000, maturities 0.03, 0.05, 0.07 and 0.09 years (the maturities of 2107.01611's data, Section 3.1), log-moneyness strikes from -0.15 to 0.05
pass: put-call parity within 3 Monte Carlo standard errors at every strike and maturity
prices within no-arbitrage bounds (call between max(S - K, 0) and S), and decreasing and convex in strike up to Monte Carlo error
convergence: halving dt changes no price by more than 3 standard errors; quadrupling paths shrinks the standard error by about half

implied volatilities: a negative skew (higher implied volatility at lower strikes) at every maturity, as the papers' SPX smiles show, and an at-the-money level in the range of the initial volatility sqrt(V0), stated as a shape check, not a number from the papers
no NaN, positive variance on every path

rule: step 1 passes when every check passes; if any fails, step 1 stops and is reported, and step 2 does not start
data: synthetic: Monte Carlo paths of the model at the papers' parameters; no market data
